Notation: Pi(k) = k! (Gauss's notation). The page treats the case mu ≡ 0 (mod 4). It collects coefficient conditions for four families of unknowns a, b, a', b', indexed in steps of 4, which enter with binomial-type weights 1/(p! q!) where p+q is roughly mu. This is the pattern one gets by expanding a homogeneous polynomial of degree mu in two variables as sum c_p x^p y^q/(p! q!) and imposing a constant-coefficient linear system of PDEs with a parameter r. The underlying problem is not stated on the page. The previous page has similar recurrences in a parameter t (a_0=1, 4a_4=-6+2t, a_8=98-72t+12t^2, ...). The next page treats an elasticity-type boundary problem for a strip (cos sqrt(1-lambda)x, Poisson-type constant nu). The link between these is my conjecture.

(1) Lines 1-2 give the coefficient relations of degree mu-2. In them a_{mu-4n}+a_{mu-4-4n}, combined with ±(4r-2) b, carries the weight 1/((mu-2-2n)!(2n)!). Likewise b_{mu-4n}+b_{mu-4-4n}, combined with ±(4r-2) a_{mu-4-4n}, carries the weight 1/((mu-3-2n)!(2n+1)!). Adding and subtracting the two lines decouples a from b.

(2) The a-equation. Shift n -> n-1 in the terms carrying a_{mu-4-4n}. This gives
Sum_n a_{mu-4n} [ 1/((mu-2-2n)!(2n)!) + 1/((mu-2n)!(2n-2)!) - (4r-2)/((mu-1-2n)!(2n-1)!) ] = 0.
Multiply through by (mu-2n)!(2n)!. The bracket becomes
(mu-2n)(mu-2n-1) + 2n(2n-1) - (4r-2)(mu-2n)2n.
Riemann regroups this as (mu-2n)(mu-1) + 2n(mu-1) - 4r(mu-2n)2n = mu(mu-1) - 4r(mu-2n)2n. Hence
I: Sum_n a_{mu-4n} [mu(mu-1) - 4r(mu-2n)2n] / ((mu-2n)!(2n)!) = 0.
Test at mu=4: a_4·12/24 + a_0(12-16r)/(2!2!) = 0, so a_4 = (8r-6)a_0 (my evaluation).

(3) The b-equation. Put A = mu-1-2n and B = 2n+1. The bracket is -(4r-2)AB + B(B-1) + A(A-1). Since A+B = mu, this equals mu(mu-1) - 4rAB. Hence
II: Sum_n b_{mu-4n} [mu(mu-1) - 4r(mu-2n-1)(2n+1)] / ((mu-2n-1)!(2n+1)!) = 0.
Riemann tests small cases (b_6/b_2; b_4/b_0 with weights (12-12r)/3!) and writes b = 0. Presumably the b-chain starts from b_0 = 0, so the triangular recursion forces all b to vanish.

(4) Primed families, with parameter 4r+1 and index shift m = mu-4n-2. These are third-order weights. Put A = mu-2n and B = 2n. The bracket is
A(A-1)(A-2) - B(B-1)(B-2) + (4r+1)AB[(A-1)-(B-1)].
Riemann splits off 4r·AB(A-B) = 4r(mu-2n)2n(mu-4n). The rest is (mu-2)[A(A-1) - B(B-1)] = (mu-2)(mu-1)(mu-4n). This gives
III: Sum_n a'_{mu-4n} (mu-4n)[(mu-1)(mu-2) + 4r(mu-2n)2n] / ((2n)!(mu-2n)!) = 0.
The factor (mu-4n) kills the a'_0 term. So for mu=4 the relation gives a'_4·1 = 0, then a'_8 = 0, and so on. Riemann concludes a' = 0, provided the brackets do not vanish.

(5) The same computation with A = mu-2n-1 and B = 2n+1, where A-B = mu-4n-2, gives
IV: Sum_n b'_{mu-4n} (mu-4n-2)[(mu-1)(mu-2) + 4r(mu-2n-1)(2n+1)] / ((2n+1)!(mu-2n-1)!).
Riemann concludes b' = 0 after a small-case check ('2 4 3 ±').

Net content: the even/odd coefficient families satisfy closed one-parameter recursions with the compact symmetric kernels above. The primed families are forced to vanish.
errors: In the intermediate line for IV, the term (mu-2)(2n+1)(2n) should carry a minus sign: it is -(mu-2)B(B-1). The final factored form IV is nevertheless correct.
In the a'_4 check, the coefficient written '4(4.3)/(0!4!)' is effectively 4·3·2/4! = 1; the notation is garbled but the conclusion a'_4 = 0 is right.

For IV with mu=4, the formula as written gives the relation b'_4 = b'_0 (my evaluation, assuming r ≠ -1/2). So the claim b' = 0 needs an extra initial condition, presumably b'_0 = 0. The small-case scribble '2 4 3 ±' is unclear.
In line 2, the second denominator is written Pi(mu-3-2n)Pi(2n); by consistency with line 1 it should be Pi(2n+1).
